verdict_reason: On the estimand's actual domain the implementation is faithful: against the executed released Alsace08/Chain-of-Embedding score.py, 500 random chains agree to 6.66e-16 (CoE-R) and 5.55e-16 (CoE-C) in float64, and on 300 REAL chains from gpt2 / pythia-70m / distilgpt2 the shipped float32 path agrees with the float64 released scorer to a worst relative error of 2.93e-04 (CoE-R) and 2.34e-07 (CoE-C). The caveat that keeps it off GREEN is that three BLME-only guards, none of which exists in the paper or the released code, return NaN or 0 where the definition is finite: I reproduced all three, including the NEW one introduced by the round-9 relative-floor fix.
comparable_reason: CoE-R and CoE-C are explicitly depth-normalised sums of L terms over an end-to-end normaliser, so inserting identity layers halves them (L=2 -> L=4 takes R from 0.20710678118654757 to 0.10355339059327379 in BOTH BLME and the released code -- faithful, and still not comparable). Panel: coe_r 0.1209 / 0.0132 / -0.3657 / -0.1504 / 0.2706 for distilgpt2 / gpt2 / pythia-70m / pythia-160m / gpt2-medium -- the SIGN differs between architecture families, Spearman rho +0.894 with d_model. mean_angle_change is rho -0.949 with n_layers. mean_magnitude_change (49.0-98.0) is a raw hidden-state magnitude in model units. _meta_normalized_coe_c is byte-identical to coe_c on 5/5 models, so it is an alias, not a normalisation.
github_reason: Executed the released score.py CoEScoreInfo class (compute_CoE_Mag / compute_CoE_Ang / compute_CoE_R / compute_CoE_C) unchanged against BLME's _coe_from_chain on: 500 random chains (worst |dR| 6.661e-16, |dC| 5.551e-16 in float64); the three counterexamples below; and 300 real gpt2/pythia-70m/distilgpt2 chains at the last prompt token (worst relative 2.9285e-04 on R, 2.3378e-07 on C, the residual being BLME's deliberate float32 materialisation at coe.py:307 against the reference's float64 numpy). I also confirmed the chain-construction choice: BLME uses the raw HF hidden_states tuple, which is what inference.py::print_hidden_states does, and the resulting coe_r values (+0.1209 distilgpt2 / +0.0132 gpt2 / -0.3657 pythia-70m) match the reference-chain column in the file's own comment rather than the block-output column.
paper_reason: Wang et al. (arXiv:2410.13640) publish only downstream CLASSIFICATION statistics -- Table 1's AUROC / FPR95 / AUPR for correctness prediction (e.g. Llama2-7B-Instruct mathematics CoE-R 64.23 / 84.47 / 20.94). The task emits none of those three, and reproducing them needs the paper's labelled generation experiment, which is outside the small-model budget for this review. The paper is also internally inconsistent on CoE-C -- prose Eq. 6/7 uses raw M*exp(iA), Algorithm 2 normalises only the magnitude, and the released score.py normalises both -- and BLME follows the released code and says so at coe.py:180-189, which is the right resolution.
confounds_reason: By construction CoE-R and CoE-C average over L layer transitions divided by an end-to-end normaliser, so depth enters analytically (verified: identity-layer insertion from L=2 to L=4 exactly halves both, in BLME and in the released code alike). _meta_chain_length_per_sample is literally n_layers (6/12/6/12/24 in my panel, rho +1.000 with n_layers). Measured over 5 models: mean_normalized_angle rho -0.949 with n_layers and -0.900 with parameter count; coe_r rho +0.894 with d_model. The raw companions mean_magnitude_change and std_magnitude_change are unnormalised hidden-state norms.
defects: CODE / NEW REGRESSION from the round-9 fix (reproduced): coe.py:154-156 replaced the absolute z_mag <= 1e-12 test with _z_floor = 1e-12 * max|coordinate ANYWHERE IN THE CHAIN|. A large intermediate excursion therefore declares well-separated endpoints degenerate. On H = [(1,0), (1e13,1e13), (0,1)]: z_mag = 1.4142135623730951, floor = 10.0, BLME returns NaN/NaN in BOTH float32 and float64 while the executed released scorer returns R/C = 9999999999999.0 / 9999999999999.5. The old absolute floor did not have this failure; the fix traded one unreachable failure for another. Correct behaviour is no floor at all -- divide whenever z_mag > 0 -- exactly as the released code does.

CODE / BLME-ONLY ANGLE SNAP: coe.py:83-86 returns exactly 0.0 when cos >= 1 - 1e-12 and exactly pi when cos <= -1 + 1e-12, which erases every angle below sqrt(2e-12) = 1.414e-06 rad. On unit vectors at angles (0, 5e-7, 1.5e-6) BLME gives R/C = 0.5000000000000313 / 0.5000000000000313 against the released -2.467125547267468e-05 / 0.49384563092475414. Measured margin on real data: the smallest adjacent-layer angle over 300 real chains is 0.1058 rad (pythia-70m), 4.9 orders above the threshold, so no shipped number moves.

CODE / OVERFLOW BEFORE PROMOTION: coe.py:130/:134 subtract in the chain's float32 dtype and only then hand the result to _norm2's double fallback, so an already-infinite difference cannot be repaired. s*[(1,0),(0,1),(-1,0)] has finite float32 coordinates at s = 2.406159650500376e38 and 3.4028234663852886e38 but BLME returns NaN/NaN where the released code returns 0.20710678118654757 / 0.7071067811865476. It is correct at 1e25.

REACHABILITY, in the code's favour: over 300 real chains the smallest z_mag / chain_scale ratio is 0.9495 (gpt2), 11.98 orders above the 1e-12 guard, and the median is 1.09-6.63. All three defects above are therefore analytic-domain only on transformer activations.

PROTOCOL, disclosed: the released code pools h^(l) across every GENERATED token from model.generate; BLME reads the last PROMPT token with no generation (num_samples=100, token_position=last in the merged study config). The docstring says so.
TEST GAP: neither tests/test_scale_invariance.py nor tests/tasks/test_centre_and_rescale.py contains a CoE case, so nothing in the suite can see any of the three guards above.
fix: Delete the chain-wide relative magnitude floor (a finite nonzero endpoint distance is never degenerate) and the 1e-12 cosine snap (clamp to [-1,1] and take arccos, as the released code does); form chain differences after promotion so an overflowed intermediate never reaches _norm2.
